purpose: Resolve source-specific NFL team abbreviations to the canonical team_code in the Gameplan NFL team registry, before anything crosses the production boundary.
rationale: This is the team analogue of the GSIS rule. Gameplan decision 3 requires the provider to resolve player identity upstream because the consumer must never guess; team identity is the same problem with a smaller key space, and the same answer. Every alias here was found by a run silently producing a wrong result rather than an error: the Rams came back with zero defensive scores because play-by-play writes LA where the registry writes LAR, and every record still validated. Prefix matching is not safe -- LA is a prefix of LAC as well as LAR, and JAC/JAX share no useful prefix rule. Enumerate, do not infer.

LA.note: nflverse play-by-play and weekly releases write LA for the Los Angeles Rams. LAC is written in full, so LA is unambiguous in this dataset -- but only in this dataset.

JAC.note: CBS Sports writes JAC for Jacksonville; the registry and nflverse write JAX.

ARZ.note: Ourlads writes ARZ for Arizona, in its team index and in its depth-chart URL; the registry, nflverse and depth-charts/NFC_WEST/ARI.json all write ARI. The alias was previously attributed to pro_scout_manifest, because the foreign spelling had been allowed to propagate into this repo's own records -- manifest/depth-charts.json, manifest/team-state.json and the team_state_id NFL:2026:ARZ. Those are canonical as of this commit, so this entry now covers only what Ourlads publishes, which is what an alias is for. Ourlads' own URL keeps ARZ: it is their address, not our code.
